name: PIVCO-Huffman (pivco-huffman)
baseline: huf0 (zstd's Huffman decoder from FiniteStateEntropy, X1 single-symbol and X2 double-symbol variants) and an in-tree traditional 4-stream table Huffman decoder; Oodle Huffman (oo-huff) is wired into bench/bench_fair.c only when an Oodle SDK is linked and does not appear in the BENCHMARKS.md tables
workload: Decode of a 4M-symbol Huffman-coded block sequence repeated 100 times (400M symbols per run), 5 runs, median of 3 best; synthetic distributions (proba80, flat, zipfian, ...) and real files (html_wiki, english, json_api, source_c, ...).
claimed_speedup: Apple M4 Max: proba80 15,339 MB/s vs huf0 X2 2,617 (5.91x best-of-others); real text 4.3-4.8 GB/s, 2.0-2.5x huf0_x2; Xeon 6975P-C AVX-512: english 7,909 vs huf0 X2 1,875 (4.22x), html_wiki 4,765 (2.96x), proba80 22,581 (11.70x). Encoded size within 1-4% of traditional Huffman.
compiler_and_flags: GCC 11.5.0 on Amazon Linux 2023 for the Xeon 6975P-C (c8i) and Graviton 4 (c8g) tables, clang-20 for the AMD EPYC 7R13 Zen 3 (c6a) table; CMakeLists.txt adds -Wall -Wextra -O3 and, on AVX-512 hosts, -mavx512f -mavx512bw -mavx512vl -mavx512vbmi -mavx512vbmi2 -mavx512vpopcntdq -mavx2 -mbmi2 -msse4.1 -mpopcnt (AVX2 hosts: -mavx2 -mbmi2 -msse4.1 -mpopcnt); Apple M4 compiler not stated
hardware: Apple M4 Max (NEON, block 8192); Intel Xeon 6975P-C AVX-512 VBMI2 (AWS c8i, 2 vCPU); AWS Graviton 4 Neoverse V2 (c8g.large, taskset -c 0); AMD EPYC 7R13 Zen 3 AVX2/SSE4.1 (AWS c6a, 2 vCPU, block 4096)
tradeoffs: Not a drop-in: new bitstream (PivCo partition bitmaps), block-based (4096-8192 symbol blocks), encoder walks the Huffman tree; needs SIMD with permute/compress primitives (NEON, AVX-512 VBMI2, AVX2). Encoded size 1-4% above traditional Huffman. PHA variant adds FSE/ANS coded bitmaps for better ratio on skewed data at lower decode speed.
caveats: README marks the project as WIP and not production-ready; co-authored with an AI assistant per commit trailers. BENCHMARKS.md is a 2026-05-15 snapshot marked 'Last content review: NEVER'. On Zen 3 (SSE/AVX2) html_wiki, json_api and log_apache lose to huf0 X2 at 0.94-0.95x and several rows are only 1.06-1.3x; Graviton 4 real text is 1.29-1.47x. flat_M7 on M4 is only 1.43x. The README TL;DR's real-text range (4.3-4.8 GB/s, 2.0-2.5x) does not include the M4 table's english row (6142 MB/s, 2.55x). In-memory decode-only microbenchmark; huf0 uses 128 KB chunks while PIVCO uses 4096-8192-symbol blocks; tables use the --no-fse (PH) configuration. Paper (PDF on github.io) and arXiv copy not opened (hosts blocked).

tradeoffs: FSE is a table-based tANS coder (precise like arithmetic coding, but slower than Huff0); Huff0 is Huffman with 4-stream interleaving, loses ratio on skewed distributions (cannot go below 1 bit per symbol). Both are block-oriented with a header describing the distribution.

name: Rapidgzip
baseline: GNU gzip (single-threaded deflate decoder); also compared with pigz, igzip (ISA-L), bgzip and pzstd
workload: Decompression of arbitrary gzip files (Silesia tar repeated 20x, 3.95 GiB; 4 GiB base64 data) on a Ryzen 3900X, plus scaling to 128 cores on 2x EPYC 7702.
claimed_speedup: Ryzen 3900X, 20x-silesia with existing index: 5640 MB/s (0 threads=auto) vs gzip 293 MB/s (18.8x); from scratch 2070 MB/s (6.9x); 4GiB-base64 from scratch 5060 MB/s vs gzip 250 MB/s (20.1x). README: up to 24 GB/s with index and 12 GB/s without on 128 cores; 24.3 GB/s vs 9.5 GB/s for pzstd with index. Paper abstract: 5.6 GB/s on Silesia, speedup 33 over GNU gzip, with 128 cores. README: single-core decompression close to igzip and about twice as fast as bgzip (zlib).
license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT (repo page lists both; per-file split not checked)
tradeoffs: Multi-core only wins: single-thread speed is close to igzip, not faster. Needs memory for chunk cache and a two-stage decode of unknown windows; with an index it reaches higher bandwidth. Read-only decompressor (compression is delegated to other tools). C++17, usable as header-only C++ library.
caveats: Peer-reviewed (ACM HPDC 2023, DOI 10.1145/3588195.3592992); the paper PDF in mxmlnkn/indexed_bzip2/results/paper was opened, but neither it nor the README states the compiler or flags. The headline gain is parallel scaling versus single-threaded GNU gzip, not a faster single-thread inflate: in the paper (rapidgzip 0.5.0), single-threaded rapidgzip reached 153 MB/s, while bgzip was 1.9x and igzip 4.3x as fast; the README's claim that single-core speed is close to igzip refers to later versions. Baseline is GNU gzip rather than zlib. The README scaling plots used rapidgzip 0.9.0, and its values are higher than the paper's. The paper's text gives GNU gzip on Silesia as "172 GB/s", an evident typo for MB/s.

The 22.7 GB/s headline compares 8-thread Glyd decoding with single-thread zstd/LZ4 frame decoding. name: rankselect (PTSelect, splatlab)
workload: Rank and select queries on uncompressed bit vectors, plus select on single 64-bit words using PDEP and TZCNT (PTSelect); the repo has bitmap_bench.cc and bitmap_bench_sdsl.cc that time the same queries on this code and on SDSL.
claimed_speedup: Snippet only (arXiv 1706.00990, not opened): PTSelect, a 4-instruction machine-word select (PDEP + TZCNT), is 2x-4x faster than the previous state-of-the-art 64-bit word select; select on bit vectors is 2.2x-6x faster than CS-Poppy and SDSL.
compiler_and_flags: Makefile: g++ -std=c++11 -O9 -mpopcnt -msse4 -I. -Iinclude/ -Iinclude/sdsl
tradeoffs: Select via PDEP needs a Haswell-or-later x86 CPU (BMI2). Rank/select over uncompressed bit sequences only. Bundles an old copy of SDSL headers for the comparison.
caveats: Speedup numbers come only from search snippets of arXiv preprint 1706.00990 (arXiv and a third-party summary blog are blocked here). The README is one line with no numbers, and no CPU model appears in the repo. The repo is a GitHub fork of efficient/rankselect (CMU's CS-Poppy code, Apache-2.0, copyright 2013 CMU); this fork adds PTSelect (select64_pdep_tzcnt in popcount.h, used by select64) and the SDSL benchmark. It needs a Haswell-or-later CPU with BMI2, although the Makefile passes only -mpopcnt -msse4 because PDEP/TZCNT come in through inline asm. Timing uses gettimeofday. It bundles an older SDSL version (2017). Newer work (pasta bit_vector, sux) is already catalogued and likely faster. Preprint; peer-review status not verified.

SDSL rank_support_v is not the most compact SDSL rank (v5 has less space), and sux, pasta, poppy and SPIDER were not compared. The SDSL space figure excludes the select_support_mcl directory.
